I picked B on physical reasoning, because the data can't separate the two directions.

In the data, the correlation between `Residual_shortwave` and `Residual_GH_mean` is about -0.03, so there is no strong linear link either way. A correlation can't show which variable drives the other, and I didn't run a causal-direction test.

Physically, geopotential height reflects atmospheric circulation. A high-pressure ridge brings clearer skies, which changes the net shortwave radiation reaching the surface. Surface shortwave flux has little direct effect on large-scale geopotential height. So the more plausible direction is Residual_GH_mean causing Residual_shortwave.

ANSWER: B
